tier_reason: The only numbers come from yaysummeriscoming/xnnpack_benchmarks, a 1-star, 4-commit personal harness (not a well-known independent suite, no paper); its scripts are public but the CPU model, compiler and flags are not stated and the two engines ran different model files, so it falls short of A and does not qualify for B (precedent: small personal suites tiered C).

corrections.claimed_speedup: Single thread (the first table; the scripts pass --nthreads 1 / --num_threads=1): ResNet 50 OpenVINO latency-optimized 62.55 ms vs TFLite+XNNPACK 118.3 ms (about 1.9x, derived from page data); MobileNet V2 11.14 vs 11.48 ms (tie). 8 threads: ResNet 50 16.70 vs 32.8 ms (about 2.0x, derived from page data); MobileNet V2 3.56 vs 3.16 ms (XNNPACK faster). OpenVINO throughput-optimized mode: MobileNet V2 382.44 FPS (at 10.40 ms latency) vs 316.46 FPS for XNNPACK; ResNet 50 67.73 vs 30.49 FPS.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: TFLite benchmark_model built from TensorFlow master with 'bazel build -c opt' (Bazel 3.0.0; compiler not stated); OpenVINO 2020.3.194 prebuilt apt runtime with benchmark_app built by build_samples.sh; no compiler versions or flags stated
corrections.caveats: The benchmark is a small personal repository (1 star, 4 commits, GPL-3.0, undated; OpenVINO 2020.3.194 and TensorFlow master built with Bazel 3.0.0, i.e. about 2020) with an unstated CPU model, so it falls short of tier A and is not an established suite. The engines did not run the same model files: OpenVINO used Open Model Zoo Caffe MobileNet V2 / ResNet-50 converted to FP32 IR, while TFLite+XNNPACK used Keras-built models modified for XNNPACK (explicit padding layers and the global-average-pool mean op removed, weights=None). OpenVINO wins on ResNet 50 but ties at 1 thread and loses at 8 threads on MobileNet V2 latency. A separate user report (XNNPACK issue 1803, Aug 2021, EC2 T2.Large, MobileNet V1 and AlexNet) says OpenVINO took 50% of XNNPACK's latency, but it got no maintainer reply and is anecdotal.

notes: All numbers match the benchmark README; the 'thread count not labelled' first table is single-threaded per run_benchmarks_openvino.sh and run_benchmarks_xnnpack.sh. Downgraded B to C because the source is a 1-star personal harness with mismatched model inputs. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0, 10.9k stars, last commit 2026-10-01.

tier_reason: First-party README tables (A100, CUDA 11.6) with no host CPU or compiler flags; the public script benchmark/bert_bench.sh times only ByteTransformer (via unit_test/python_scripts/bert_transformer_test.py), so the PyTorch, TensorFlow, FasterTransformer and DeepSpeed columns have no public harness. The IPDPS 2023 paper (arXiv 2210.03052) could not be opened (arxiv.org blocked here), so no upgrade to B.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: CUDA 11.6 nvcc via CMake (-DDataType=FP16, CUDAARCHS=80, -rdc=true); build type, optimisation level and host compiler not stated
corrections.hardware: NVIDIA A100 GPU (variant and host CPU not stated); CUDA 11.6, PyTorch 1.13.0+cu116, Python 3.9.16
corrections.workload: Standard BERT encoder (12 layers, 12 heads x 64, fp16 per benchmark/bert_bench.sh) execution time (ms) on an A100 at batch 1 and batch 16, sequence lengths 64 to 1024, average length 0.6 of maximum.
corrections.caveats: First-party README numbers. The public benchmark script benchmark/bert_bench.sh only times ByteTransformer (fp16, 12 layers); the baseline framework timings cannot be reproduced from the repository, and compiler flags and host CPU are not stated. The IEEE IPDPS 2023 paper (arXiv 2210.03052) was not opened. ByteTransformer is not always fastest: at batch 1, FasterTransformer is ahead at sequence 192-384 (1.26 vs 1.36, 1.35 vs 1.43, 1.63 vs 1.69, 1.64 vs 1.72 ms); at batch 16, FasterTransformer with remove-padding wins at sequence 64 (1.93 vs 2.09 ms) and 256-384 (5.49 vs 6.85, 6.47 vs 7.49, 7.05 vs 8.44 ms). Gains are largest at long sequences with batch 16 (padding-free path). Baselines are frameworks and FasterTransformer, not cuDNN, so it is not shown to beat cuDNN kernels directly. Only BERT encoder supported; last commit March 2024.

notes: All claimed numbers match the README tables; added the batch-16 sequence 256-384 cases where FasterTransformer with remove-padding beats ByteTransformer, which the record missed. A WebSearch snippet says the paper was accepted at IPDPS 2023 and reports 6.13x fused-MHA vs PyTorch; the paper itself was not opened. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0, 481 stars, not archived, last commit 2024-03-15 (stale).

tier_reason: First-party README benchmark tables (CPU on c5.2xlarge Xeon Platinum 8275CL, GPU on g5.xlarge A10G) with public Docker-based scripts in tools/benchmark, but no compiler or flags (prebuilt packages), so not A; no independent or peer-reviewed source.

corrections.caveats: First-party README numbers measured with CTranslate2 3.6.0 (the current release is 4.8.x, so the published table is stale) against PyTorch 1.13.1, TensorFlow 2.11.0, Transformers 4.26.1, Marian 1.11.0 and FasterTransformer 5.3; public Docker-based benchmark scripts in tools/benchmark, but no compiler or flags and prebuilt packages. Baselines are whole frameworks, not oneDNN, cuDNN, XNNPACK or Eigen kernels, so this does not show a kernel-level win over them. Like-for-like quantized comparisons are smaller than the headline: CPU int8 CTranslate2 860.2 vs OpenNMT-py int8 323.3 tok/s, and CTranslate2 int8 696.1 vs Marian int8 355.8 tok/s. FasterTransformer fp32 was faster than CTranslate2 fp32 on the GPU (6979.0 vs 6634.7 tok/s). The README itself warns relative performance changes with settings. Tokenization, detokenization and model loading are excluded from the timed region.

notes: All claimed numbers match the README Benchmarks section. Metadata checked: MIT, 4.7k stars, not archived, last commit 2026-09-26.
